databaseName: Section 8 - Building Generative AI Applications with Bedrock

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is a Foundation Model and how are they used?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Foundation models are pre-trained large models such as Titan or Claude that can be used directly or extended to support specific applications.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: ________ are pre-trained models such as Titan and Claude that can be extended to support applications.
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Foundation models are pre-trained models such as Titan and Claude that can be extended to support applications.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What makes Titan special?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Titan is AWS's own foundation model. While it still requires approval, approval is much quicker and there is no third-party billing or external terms involved.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Which model is AWS's own foundation model with quicker approval and no third-party billing?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Titan.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Is Amazon Bedrock serverless?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Yes, Amazon Bedrock is serverless.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are the four Bedrock API groups?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: The four API groups are: manage chat/continuation, execute chat/continuation (Converse, ConverseStream, InvokeModel, InvokeModelWithResponseStream), manage agents, and execute agents (InvokeAgent, Retrieve, RetrieveAndGenerate).

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are the two most important Bedrock IAM permissions?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Users must use an IAM user (not the root account) and have appropriate Bedrock permissions, most commonly AmazonBedrockFullAccess or AmazonBedrockFullReadonly. Admin roles may have these implicitly.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Discuss fine-tuning: what it is and how it is used.
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Fine-tuning adapts an existing LLM to a specific use case by extending the model through additional training. It reduces reliance on prompt engineering, can save tokens long-term, allows iterative improvement, and supports applications like custom chatbots, updated knowledge, proprietary data usage, and classification tasks. It can be more expensive upfront.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: The following description refers to which concept?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Fine-tuning.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is a custom model?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: A custom model is a model that has been fine-tuned.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What does AWS call fine-tuning?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: AWS refers to fine-tuning as creating a custom model.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is a reason a model cannot be fine-tuned?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Only certain models support fine-tuning. According to the lecture, Titan, Cohere, and Meta models support it on AWS, while other models such as OpenAI models may support fine-tuning outside AWS.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: In fine-tuning a model, how do we keep proprietary data secure?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: By using a VPC and AWS PrivateLink.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are some disadvantages of fine-tuning?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Fine-tuning can be expensive upfront, time-consuming, and requires providing high-quality training data.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is continued pre-training?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Continued pre-training extends a model using unlabeled data by feeding it additional text so the knowledge becomes part of the model itself, reducing the need to include that data in prompts.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is the difference between fine-tuning and continued pre-training?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Fine-tuning uses labeled prompt-response data, while continued pre-training uses unlabeled fact-style data to extend the model's knowledge.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: How can a model's knowledge be extended with new or proprietary data without training?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: By using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which retrieves relevant data at inference time rather than training the model on it.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: How do you perform a semantic search?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: By embedding the query into a vector and performing a nearest-neighbor search against vectors stored in a knowledge base.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are the pros of RAG?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: RAG is faster and cheaper than fine-tuning in the short term, easy to update, supports semantic search with vector stores, can reduce hallucinations, enables AI search use cases, and avoids training on proprietary data.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: The following describes the advantages of which technique?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are the cons of RAG?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: RAG can behave like a poor search engine, is highly sensitive to chunking and prompt templates, is non-deterministic, can still hallucinate, and depends heavily on the quality of retrieved data.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Discuss cost tradeoffs between fine-tuning and RAG.
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Fine-tuning has higher upfront costs but may reduce future token usage. RAG has no training cost but increases ongoing token usage due to added context.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is an embedding?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: An embedding is a high-dimensional vector representation of text or data used for semantic comparison.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is the basic flow of semantic search?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Documents are embedded into vectors, stored, queries are embedded, nearest neighbors are retrieved, relevant documents are added to the prompt, and the augmented prompt is sent to the model.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: The search results in semantic search are similar to which algorithm?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN).

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: How do we store vectors and what does AWS recommend?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Vectors are stored in vector stores or databases with vector search support. AWS typically recommends OpenSearch or Elasticsearch.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Comment on the structure of data required for Bedrock knowledge bases.
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Bedrock can accept structured or unstructured data, but default chunking may not perform well. Proper chunking strategy is important.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What alternative data sources can be used for knowledge bases?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Data can come from web crawlers, Jira, SNS/SQS, Salesforce, or any source that can land data in S3.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are the key activities in knowledge base search?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Embedding data, storing vectors, embedding queries, performing vector search, and adding results to prompts.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What kinds of data can be used in a knowledge base?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Text, spreadsheets, images, audio, PDFs, and other data types.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What data sources can be used for Bedrock knowledge bases?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: S3, web crawlers, Salesforce, and custom sources.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What data structure is required for Bedrock knowledge bases?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Bedrock can parse both structured and unstructured data using default, inferred, or custom parsers.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What chunking strategies are available in Bedrock?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Default chunking, fixed-size chunking, hierarchical chunking, semantic chunking, no chunking, and custom Lambda-based chunking.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What guardrail features are available in Bedrock?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Content filtering (words, topics, PII, profanity), context grounding checks, and blocked message responses.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is context grounding check?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: It evaluates grounding against retrieved content and relevance to the query using configurable thresholds.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: For agents, what is memory?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Agents have no persistent memory; the full conversation context is sent with each prompt and acts as memory.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: How does an agent know which tool to call and with what parameters?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Tool and parameter descriptions define their purpose, types, and requirements, allowing the agent to determine which to invoke.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is the recommended tool provider for agents?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: AWS Lambda is commonly used and promoted as a suitable tool provider depending on the use case.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are action groups?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Action groups are collections of tools or functions used by agents.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: How are functions defined for agents?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Functions are defined using an OpenAPI-style schema that specifies function names, descriptions, parameter types, and required fields.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: How is RAG implemented with agents?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: RAG is implemented as a tool call, similar to other agent tools.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is the code interpreter tool used for in agents?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: It allows agents to write and execute code, although the exact execution environment may depend on implementation.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: How are agents billed and which model is best for different workloads?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: On-demand throughput is suited for low to normal usage, while provisioned throughput is best for high-volume workloads requiring guaranteed token capacity.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is InvokeAgent and what parameter is required?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: InvokeAgent is the API method used to call an agent and requires an agent alias ID in addition to the prompt.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are the additional features of Bedrock?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Additional features include imported models, model evaluation (automatic and human), provisioned throughput, watermark detection, and Bedrock Studio.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Does Bedrock limit which foundation models you can use?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Bedrock does not strictly limit models but restricts which providers it partners with. You can also bring your own models.

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: How can Bedrock be used to evaluate models?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Through automatic metrics such as accuracy, toxicity, robustness, BERTScore, and F1, as well as human evaluation using your own team or AWS-managed teams.
